curation.notes: Custom dual-trap optical tweezers force-extension (constant-velocity pulling) of single prion protein (PrP 90-231) molecules from dog, hamster and bank vole, each tethered via cysteine-linked DNA handles; folding intermediates, pathways and barriers compared across species. Includes all-atom MD of candidate intermediate substructures.

evidence.snippet: Data were sampled at 20 kHz and filtered online with an eight-pole Bessel filter (Krohn-Hite) at the Nyquist frequency.

filter_frequency.note: Nyquist frequency of 20 kHz sampling = 10 kHz; auto value of 20000 Hz was wrong

evidence.snippet: Data were sampled at 20 kHz and filtered online with an eight-pole Bessel filter (Krohn-Hite) at the Nyquist frequency.
The trap stiffnesses were 0.37 and 0.56 pN/nm, calibrated by three independent means (extension variance, extension power spectral density, and viscous drag) as described (82).

bead_size.note: 600 nm avidin beads and 820 nm anti-digoxigenin beads

evidence.snippet: 250 pM polystyrene beads (600-nm diameter functionalized with avidin, 820-nm diameter functionalized with anti-digoxigenin) to form dumbbells

attachment_chemistry: cysteine–DTDP-activated disulfide to sulfhydryl-labelled DNA handle

evidence.snippet: pulling speeds of 125 to 250 nm/s for CaPrP and BvPrP, 20-230 nm/s for HaPrP

handle_sequences.annotations: for CaPrP and BvPrP: one of length 802 bp labeled with biotin
the other of length 2,100 bp labeled with digoxigenin
for HaPrP, 798 bp labeled with biotin

evidence.snippet: Samples of PrP from each species, with sequence truncated to residues 90–231 (forming the protease-resistant core of PrPSc), were expressed recombinantly in Escherichia coli

mutations: Cys added at both termini for handle attachment
